annotation.authors_or_issuer: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
key_provisions_or_claims: Calls for people-centered, fairness, inclusive and collaborative AI governance with balance between development and security
Advocates risk-oriented agile governance, tiered and category-based management, and AI remaining under human control
AI agents must have defined decision authority, behavioral boundaries, tracing and risk alert mechanisms
Supports UN central role, UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance and Independent International Scientific Panel on AI
Signing of agreement establishing World AI Cooperation Organization (WAICO) in Shanghai; capacity-building for Global South
annotation.summary_en: Chair's statement from the 2026 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance in Shanghai. It sets out fifteen points on innovation, openness, data, sustainability, security, AI agents, UN-centered multilateralism, standards and capacity-building for the Global South, and notes signing of the WAICO founding agreement.
